research.summary:
Efferent is real, and only one project uses the name: the PyPI package "efferent" (latest 0.5.0, Apache-2.0), developed at github.com/Eximius-Labs/efferent. I read the repo at commit f51e1af953afe1016dae9ceeff2b5328fa51781d. The 0.5.0 wheel's efferent/ source is byte-identical to src/efferent at that commit (after line-ending normalisation). The package is pure Python (py3-none-any) and needs numpy, pydantic, pyyaml, onnx and onnxruntime. MuJoCo is an optional extra that is imported only when the MuJoCo backend is used. Resolving efferent[mujoco] for CPython 3.13 on win_amd64 with --only-binary :all: succeeds, so nothing has to compile and cmake is not needed. I found no Linux-only dependency in the Go2 path.

The repo contains examples/go2_walk/. The policy is not downloaded at run time: go2_walk.app ships in git as a zip holding manifest.yaml and policy.onnx (758424 bytes), and it is not a Git LFS pointer. That ONNX is a conversion of rl_sar's bundled Go2 robot_lab policy. The policy.pt kept next to it has the same sha256 as fan-ziqi/rl_sar policy/go2/robot_lab/policy.pt at commit 376d42c9. rl_sar is Apache-2.0, and its README says the policy was trained with robot_lab (Isaac Lab / IsaacSim).

The MuJoCo model is Unitree's official unitree_mujoco unitree_robots/go2/scene.xml, which includes go2.xml plus 16 OBJ meshes (BSD-3-Clause). It is not committed; examples/fetch_models.py downloads it from the unpinned main branch. These files have not changed since 2024-04-29.

The policy interface:
- Observation: 45 values. ang_vel×0.25, projected gravity, the command [vel_x, vel_y, yaw_rate]×1, joint_pos−default, joint_vel×0.05 and the previous action. Joint order is FR, FL, RR, RL (hip, thigh, calf). Observations are clipped to ±100.
- Action: 12 joint position deltas. Target = default + action×[0.125, 0.25, 0.25]×4, with the action clipped to ±100. The default pose is [0, 0.8, −1.5]×4.
- PD gains: kp 20, kd 0.5. Gains for the startup phase are kp 80, kd 3.
- Torque limit: 23.5 Nm. Efferent enforces it only by scaling kp; the kd term is not limited.
- Timing: the policy runs at 50 Hz. The MJCF does not set a timestep, so MuJoCo's default 0.002 s applies, giving 10 physics substeps per policy step. PD torques are applied through qfrc_applied, so the model's actuators are not used.

The command interface is a Python callable command_source(t) that returns Command(names=[vel_x, vel_y, yaw_rate], values=float32[3]). Units are m/s and rad/s. Efferent itself does not clamp the values. robot_lab's current Go2 training ranges are ±1 for each, but the commit the policy was trained at is unknown.

The validate script never opens a viewer, so it runs headless. I did not run anything or load any checkpoint, as the rules require. The verdict rests on the source files.

Inside policy.pt there is a member policy/code/__torch__/isaaclab_rl/rsl_rl/exporter.py, which indicates export with Isaac Lab's rsl_rl exporter. The manifest records the provenance as 'trained_in: unknown', 'repo: imported-from-rl_sar', 'commit: null'. The efferent repo contains no conversion script.

claims.claim:
Go2 MJCF details (go2.xml):
- Line 4: <option> sets only cone and impratio, and scene.xml sets no timestep, so MuJoCo's default timestep of 0.002 s applies.
- Line 64: base_link starts at z 0.445 and has a freejoint.
- Joint order in the kinematic tree is FL, FR, RL, RR (hip, thigh, calf). The SDK/policy order is FR, FL, RR, RL; efferent binds joints by name.
- Joint defaults: damping 0.1, armature 0.01, frictionloss 0.2.
- Motor ctrlrange is ±23.7 for hip and thigh and ±45.43 for the knee. Efferent does not use these actuators, because it writes qfrc_applied.
- Sensors include imu framequat and gyro.
- Ranges: abduction ±1.0472, front hip -1.5708..3.4907, back hip -0.5236..4.5379, knee -2.7227..-0.83776.

claims.claim:
Observation vector: 45 values, in this order and with these scales:
- [0:3] base_ang_vel (body frame) ×0.25
- [3:6] projected_gravity = quat_rotate_inverse(quat_wxyz, [0, 0, -1]) ×1.0
- [6:9] command [vel_x, vel_y, yaw_rate] ×[1.0, 1.0, 1.0]
- [9:21] joint_pos_rel = q − default ×1.0
- [21:33] joint_vel ×0.05
- [33:45] last_action, the previous raw action after the ±100 clip ×1.0
The joint blocks use policy order FR_hip, FR_thigh, FR_calf, FL_hip, FL_thigh, FL_calf, RR_hip, RR_thigh, RR_calf, RL_hip, RL_thigh, RL_calf. history=1 for every term, there is no normalization file, and the whole vector is clipped to ±100 before inference. On the rl_sar side, num_observations is 45 and the order is ang_vel, gravity_vec, commands, dof_pos, dof_vel, actions.

claims.claim: PD gains: while the policy runs, kp = 20.0 and kd = 0.5 on all 12 joints (manifest gains). During settle, soft-start and estop the descriptor's safe gains apply: safe_kp = 80.0 and safe_kd = 3.0 on all 12 joints. The backend computes tau = kp(q_des − q) + kd(dq_des − dq) + tau_ff at every physics substep and writes it to qfrc_applied, so the model's ctrl stays at 0.

claims.claim: Torque limit is 23.5 Nm on all 12 joints. pos_limit and vel_limit are null in the descriptor. Efferent enforces the limit only by lowering kp wherever kp × |q_des − q| would exceed 23.5. The kd term is not limited, so the applied torque can exceed 23.5 Nm. rl_sar instead clamps the total PD torque to torque_limits.

claims.claim: Control rate and timestep: the policy runs at 50 Hz (0.02 s period). This comes from rl_sar's base.yaml (dt 0.005 × decimation 4) via the importer. The MuJoCo backend uses substeps = round(control_dt / model.opt.timestep) = round(0.02 / 0.002) = 10, so physics runs at 500 Hz. Training used Isaac Lab sim.dt = 0.005 with decimation 4 (robot_lab HEAD), so the sim timestep differs from training.

claims.claim:
Run sequence in the validation example:
1. Spawn the base at [0, 0, 0.35] with the joints at the default pose, then apply auto_base_height.
2. Settle for 1.0 s: 50 control steps of PD hold with the safe gains.
3. Soft start for 3.0 s: 150 steps interpolating to the default pose with the safe gains.
4. Run the policy for duration_s = 8 s: int(8.0 / 0.02) = 400 steps with command vel_x = 0.4.
The script passes if max tilt < 45°, final z > 0.15 m, x > 0.5 × commanded distance, and there is no estop.

1. Use a uv environment on Python 3.13, wheels only (--no-build): efferent==0.5.0 and mujoco==3.11.0. mujoco 3.11.0 was the release current when efferent 0.5.0 shipped; mujoco 4.0.1 also resolves but is untested with efferent. Nothing compiles, so cmake is not needed.
2. Fetch the policy and descriptor from GitHub at efferent commit f51e1af953afe1016dae9ceeff2b5328fa51781d: examples/go2_walk/go2_walk.app and examples/go2_walk/go2.robot.yaml. The PyPI artifacts do not contain them.
3. Fetch the Go2 model from Unitree's unitree_mujoco at commit 1eb6642e3f3fdfb7fb13a9794fd6a2dd93ea0e7d: unitree_robots/go2/go2.xml, scene.xml and the 16 assets/*.obj files, keeping the layout go2_model/scene.xml, go2_model/go2.xml and go2_model/assets/*.obj. Pin this commit instead of running fetch_models.py, which downloads from main and also pulls the G1 model.
4. In Python, build the pieces:
   - `m, onnx_path, _ = load_policy(app)`
   - `b = Binding(m, load_descriptor(yaml))`
   - `be = MujocoBackend(model_xml=scene, control_dt=0.02, base_pos=[0, 0, 0.35], start_pose={j.name: j.default for j in m.joints}, auto_base_height=True, settle_s=1.0)`
   - `Runner(b, PolicySession(m, onnx_path), be, command_source=fn).run(duration_s, soft_start=True)`
5. The external command chooser plugs in as `fn(t) -> Command(names=['vel_x', 'vel_y', 'yaw_rate'], values=np.float32[3])` in m/s, m/s and rad/s. Runner calls it every 20 ms. Keep values within about ±1, the robot_lab training range at its current HEAD; efferent itself does not clamp.
6. Runner.run() blocks until the duration ends; there is no public single-step API. Feed the chooser through shared state read by the callable, or reimplement the loop (ObsBuilder plus PolicySession.step plus the joint_position_delta mapping plus backend.write). It is about 20 lines; the layouts are in the claims.
7. Rendering is off by default, so no display or GL is needed.

research.proof_expected_output:
Success means sha256sum -c prints nothing (all 20 files match), uv installs wheels without building anything, and the script exits with code 0. Its last four lines should look like this:

versions efferent=0.5.0 mujoco=3.11.0 onnxruntime=1.32.0
timestep=0.002 substeps=10 rate_hz=50.0 obs_dim=45 act_dim=12 steps=400
estopped=False x=<about 1.9>m z=<above 0.15>m max_tilt=<about 15>deg wall=<N>s for 12s sim
E1 PROOF: PASS

The README reports 1.9 m and 14.7°, but with an unrecorded MuJoCo version, so small differences are expected. The script passes if x > 1.6 m (half of 0.4 m/s × 8 s, the repo's own threshold), z > 0.15 m, max tilt < 45° and there is no estop.

What a failure means:
- A sha256 mismatch: an upstream file changed.
- A pip or uv build error: a wheel is missing.
- An ONNX or MuJoCo import error: possibly the MSVC runtime is missing.
- 'E1 PROOF: FAIL': the gait does not reproduce on this machine.

A wall time well under 12 s means the sim runs faster than real time.
limitations: Following the rules, I did not run any repository code and did not load any checkpoint. Whether the Go2 example actually walks on this Windows machine is shown only by the sources and the authors' README; the proof command has not been run.

The Go2 gate does not run in efferent's CI. CI runs pytest on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS with Python 3.10-3.13, and no test touches go2. The Go2 walk was gated by Modal (Linux) scripts and is reported in the README only. The README's 'identical metrics on Windows' statement refers to the G1 jab example, not Go2.

The README says the TorchScript-to-ONNX conversion was checked for bit-level equivalence, but the repo contains no conversion script or log. Without loading both checkpoints, which is forbidden, I could not verify that policy.onnx matches rl_sar's policy.pt.

I inferred the network architecture (45 to 512 to 256 to 128 to 12) from zip member sizes, assuming float32 and storage in layer order. I did not parse the ONNX graph or its opset; only the header bytes (IR version 8, producer pytorch 2.13.0) were read.

The efferent sim differs from training in several ways:
- Physics timestep is 0.002 s (10 substeps) versus training sim.dt 0.005 s.
- Torque is limited only through kp, so the kd term can push torque above 23.5 Nm; rl_sar instead clamps the total torque.
- The gyro reading is exact free-joint angular velocity with no noise.
- Unitree's official MJCF is used, not the model the policy was trained on.
How much these affect the gait is unknown beyond the README's reported forward-walk result.
Only forward walking at 0.4 m/s is documented. Lateral and yaw commands, and other speeds, are not demonstrated anywhere in efferent.

Runner.run() blocks for the whole duration; there is no public step-by-step API. A separate command-choosing system must either plug in through the command_source(t) callable or reimplement the short control loop.

examples/fetch_models.py downloads from unitree_mujoco's unpinned 'main' branch and also fetches the G1 model. On Windows it reads the XML with Path.read_text() and the platform default encoding. The Go2 XMLs are pure ASCII, but I did not check the G1 XMLs. The proof command avoids this script by pinning the Go2 files by commit and sha256.
If mujoco is left unpinned, today's default resolution picks mujoco 4.0.1, released after efferent 0.5.0 and untested with it. The proof pins 3.11.0 instead.
I did not check whether the target machine has the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime that the onnxruntime and mujoco Windows wheels need.
open_questions: Which robot_lab commit, task config and command ranges were used to train rl_sar's policy/go2/robot_lab/policy.pt (sha256 9f14cb95...)? rl_sar has no provenance file, and the efferent manifest says 'trained_in: unknown, commit: null'. I tried: the rl_sar README, the config.yaml files, and the GitHub commit history of the policy path (the only commit found is afacc139 from 2025-10-29, a project restructure). The current robot_lab HEAD 26acb225 uses ±1.0 ranges and heading_command=True, but that may not match the training run.

Is policy.onnx numerically equivalent to policy.pt? The README claims it, but there is no script or log in the repo, and checking would require loading both files, which is out of scope for this research.
Which MuJoCo version produced the README result (1.9 m, 14.7° tilt)? It is not recorded. 3.11.0 was the newest release at efferent 0.5.0's release date, so the proof pins it.

How fast does the simulation run on the i7-7500U? Each 20 ms step is 10 mj_step calls plus a small MLP inference plus per-substep Python loops. The proof prints wall time for 12 s of simulated time, but I have not measured it.
Does the policy stay stable for non-zero vel_y or yaw_rate commands in this MuJoCo setup? This needs runs with lateral and yaw commands after the proof passes.
Is efferent compatible with mujoco 4.0.x? The changelog read lists no relevant breaking API change, but I have not tested it.

verification.summary:
I re-opened every primary source myself and did not use the researcher's copies. Sources checked: efferent cloned at f51e1af (that commit is main HEAD and tag v0.5.0); unitree_mujoco 1eb6642e, sparse clone with sizes and hashes taken from the git blobs; rl_sar 376d42c9, robot_lab 26acb225 and IsaacLab 85362ac3 read through raw URLs pinned to those commits; the MuJoCo docs at tags 3.11.0 and 4.0.1; the PyPI JSON. I also ran my own uv pip compile.

Everything the walking stack depends on matches the source, value by value and in order:
- 45-value observation: order, scales, ±100 clip, last_action taken after the action clip, and policy joint order FR, FL, RR, RL.
- Action scales [0.125, 0.25, 0.25]×4 and default pose [0, 0.8, −1.5]×4.
- Gains kp 20 / kd 0.5 while the policy runs; safe gains 80 / 3.
- Torque limit 23.5 Nm, enforced only by scaling kp.
- Timing: 50 Hz policy, timestep 0.002 s, 10 substeps, torques written to qfrc_applied.
- Run sequence: 50 settle steps, 150 soft-start steps, 400 policy steps.
- Command callable, units and robot_lab HEAD ranges; headless by default.

Files:
- All 20 proof files match their sha256 when fetched from raw URLs pinned by commit (I ran the download and sha256sum -c part only).
- All 21 wheel names, sizes, sha256 values and URLs match PyPI, about 61.4 MB in total.
- The pinned and unpinned dependency resolutions reproduce exactly.
- rl_sar policy.pt has the same sha256 as efferent's copy, base.yaml is byte-identical, and the efferent wheel source equals the repo source.
- The proof touches only the listed downloads, plus its own proof.py and an efferent_* temp directory that load_policy extracts the .app into.

Three claims contain a wrong sub-statement, none of them load-bearing:
- c1: other GitHub projects use the name "efferent".
- c18: estop is pure damping with kp 0, not kp 80.
- c19: rl_sar does not actually apply its clamped torque.

The biggest gap the report misses: Unitree's scene.xml puts obstacles and a staircase in the walking path, and the reported 1.9 m matches the robot being stopped at the first stair.

Yes. A pre-trained rl_sar Go2 policy can run on CPU inside the Python mujoco package on this machine, and every number the adapter needs is read from the rl_sar sources. The proof command has not been run yet: the rules did not allow it.

The repository is github.com/fan-ziqi/rl_sar, commit 376d42c9b128f963ab08579762d5a216a976ce39 (VERSION 4.0.0, Apache-2.0). Both candidate checkpoints exist at the paths given, and there are no Go2 .onnx files. Both are real TorchScript zip files, not LFS pointers:
- **policy/go2/himloco/himloco.pt**: 991,615 bytes, sha256 d9945f85…0509. It takes a 270-value input (6 frames x 45 observations, newest frame first) and returns 12 actions. Inside it, an estimator (270-128-64-19) feeds an actor (64-512-256-128-12).
- **policy/go2/robot_lab/policy.pt**: 769,376 bytes, sha256 9f14cb95…de0b. It takes 45 values and returns 12 actions (45-512-256-128-12, ELU activations).

rl_sar ships no Python runner. Its MuJoCo runner is C++ (src/rl_sar/src/rl_sim_mujoco.cpp) and needs cmake, which this machine does not have, but its logic is small and can be copied. At HEAD, the Go2 state machine only ever loads himloco (fsm_go2.hpp line 165), so the robot_lab Go2 policy is not exercised. Also, the robot_lab config uses kp 20 while robot_lab trains Go2 with stiffness 25.

The MJCF that rl_sar's MuJoCo runner loads (rl_sar_zoo go2_description/mjcf/go2.xml) is byte-identical, meshes included, to unitree_mujoco unitree_robots/go2/go2.xml at commit 1eb6642, which is BSD-3-Clause. The mujoco_menagerie Go2 model differs physically: joint damping 2 instead of 0.1, friction 0.6 / foot 0.8 instead of 0.4, and a different actuator order. It is not the model rl_sar validated against.

Both runtimes resolve for Python 3.13 on Windows in a uv dry run:
- mujoco==3.2.7, the MuJoCo version rl_sar pins (cp313 win_amd64 wheel, 4,760,580 bytes)
- torch==2.15.0+cpu (126,626,022 bytes); torch.jit.load still exists in v2.15.0 and only warns on Python 3.13
- onnxruntime 1.32.0 also resolves, but no ONNX file exists for Go2

**Recommendation:** himloco.pt with unitree_mujoco go2.xml.

**Main risk:** the same himloco.pt file was first deployed with a uniform action_scale of 0.25. Since v2.3 (commit 87be546) the config uses 0.125 for the hips. The proof script takes the hip scale as an argument so both can be tried.

limitations: I did not run the proof command (the task rules forbade loading checkpoints and running repository code). Whether himloco.pt actually walks with a synchronous Python MuJoCo loop is therefore unverified. rl_sar's own MuJoCo runner uses asynchronous wall-clock loops: physics at the XML default timestep of 0.002 s, PD every 5 ms and the policy every 20 ms. The recipe uses a deterministic timestep of 0.005 s with 4 substeps.

The hip action scale is ambiguous. The HEAD config says 0.125, but the byte-identical checkpoint was originally deployed with 0.25 (c17), and upstream HIMLoco Go1 uses 0.25. The recipe and proof default to the HEAD value and take 0.25 as an argument.

The proof removes the visual mesh geoms from go2.xml with a regex so that no .obj files are needed. This should not change the physics: those geoms have contype=0 and conaffinity=0, and every body has an explicit <inertial>. It also replaces the scene.xml floor and steps with a plain plane. I only checked that the edited XML is well-formed; I did not compile it with MuJoCo.
mujoco 3.2.7 (released January 2025) resolved alongside numpy 2.5.5. I assumed numpy 2 ABI compatibility and did not test it. If 'import mujoco' fails, pin an older numpy 2.x.

Licensing: himloco.pt was produced with CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 HIMLoco code and is redistributed by rl_sar without its own licence note. That is probably fine for a non-commercial hackathon, but it is not a licence grant. robot_lab policy.pt (Apache-2.0) is the clean-licence alternative, but it is not wired into any Go2 state machine at HEAD and its kp (20) differs from robot_lab's training stiffness (25).

The listed sha256 values for repository files are git blob hashes, which is what raw.githubusercontent.com serves. My local working-tree copies had CRLF line endings (core.autocrlf=true), so their text-file hashes differ.
Wheel hashes come from PyPI JSON. With --index-strategy unsafe-best-match, uv may fetch some dependencies from download.pytorch.org mirrors; I did not verify those hashes.
I used no training logs or checkpoint metadata: the command envelope, training asset and training gains for the Go2 himloco policy could not be established.
open_questions: Which hip action scale did the himloco Go2 policy train with: 0.125 (rl_sar HEAD since v2.3, 87be546) or 0.25 (the original b356b61 config for the same blob)? I checked the rl_sar git history and upstream HIMLoco (no Go2 env, Go1 uses 0.25). No Go2 HIMLoco training config is published. Settle it empirically by running the proof with both values.

What command ranges was the Go2 himloco policy trained on? rl_sar has no range config. Alternatively, strip the visual meshes with the regex '<mesh [^>]*/>|<geom [^>]*mesh="[^"]*"[^>]*/>' and append '<geom name="floor" size="0 0 0.05" type="plane"/>' to <worldbody>; this does not change the physics. Assert nu==12 and nsensordata==52.
3. Timing: set m.opt.timestep = 0.005 (config dt) and run the policy every 4 mj_step calls (decimation 4, so 50 Hz). Recompute the PD torque before every mj_step. Fallback if unstable: timestep 0.002 with 10 substeps per policy step (0.002 is the XML default rl_sar's simulator uses).
4. Index map, from config joint_mapping: JM = [3,4,5,0,1,2,9,10,11,6,7,8].
   - Joint position for policy joint i: q[i] = d.sensordata[JM[i]] (equal to d.qpos[7+i]).
   - Joint velocity: dq[i] = d.sensordata[12+JM[i]] (equal to d.qvel[6+i]).
   - Base quaternion (w,x,y,z): d.sensordata[36:40].
   - Body-frame angular velocity: d.sensordata[40:43].
   - Torque for policy joint i goes to d.ctrl[JM[i]]. Actuator order is FR,FL,RR,RL.
5. Constants (himloco config.yaml at HEAD):
   - DEF = [0.1,0.8,-1.5, -0.1,0.8,-1.5, 0.1,1.0,-1.5, -0.1,1.0,-1.5]
   - action_scale = [0.125,0.25,0.25]x4
   - kp = 40, kd = 1 (all joints)
   - commands_scale = [2.0,2.0,0.25]
   - ang_vel_scale 0.25, dof_pos_scale 1.0, dof_vel_scale 0.05
   - clip_obs 100, clip_actions ±100
6. Projected gravity: g = QuatRotateInverse(q, [0,0,-1]) with q = (w,u) and u = (x,y,z), computed as g = v*(2w²-1) - cross(u,v)*2w + u*2*dot(u,v) with v = [0,0,-1].
7. Observation (45 values, this exact order):
   - [0:3] cmd * [2.0,2.0,0.25], where cmd = [vx m/s, vy m/s, yaw rate rad/s] in the body frame
   - [3:6] gyro * 0.25
   - [6:9] g
   - [9:21] (q - DEF) * 1.0
   - [21:33] dq * 0.05
   - [33:45] last_action (the previous clipped policy output, unscaled; zeros at start)
   Then clip the whole vector to [-100,100].
8. History: a float32 buffer of shape (6,45), zero-initialised when the policy starts. Each step, shift it back by one frame and write the new observation into row 0, so the network input is the buffer flattened to shape (1,270) in order [t, t-1, …, t-5].
9. Inference: torch.set_num_threads(1); net = torch.jit.load(path, map_location='cpu').eval(); under torch.no_grad(), a = net(x)[0], giving 12 values in order P. Set a = clip(a, -100, 100) and store it as last_action.
   Torch-free alternative: read zip members policy/data/0..13 as little-endian float32 (storage map in claim c4). Then e = Lin(270→128)·ELU·Lin(128→64)·ELU·Lin(64→19); vel = e[:3]; z = e[3:19]/max(‖e[3:19]‖₂, 1e-12); a = Lin(64→512)·ELU·Lin(512→256)·ELU·Lin(256→128)·ELU·Lin(128→12) applied to concat(x[0:45], vel, z).
10. Targets: q_des = a * action_scale + DEF, with velocity target 0.
11. PD on every physics substep, using fresh q and dq: tau = 40*(q_des - q) - 1*dq, then d.ctrl[JM] = tau. Do not add a clamp: MuJoCo clamps ctrl to the actuator ctrlrange (±23.7 hip and thigh, ±45.43 calf), which is exactly what rl_sar's simulator does. The config torque_limits of 33.5 is not applied there.
12. Start-up:
   - d.qpos[0:7] = [0,0,0.35,1,0,0,0] and d.qpos[7:19] = DEF (qpos order equals P); then mj_forward.
   - Hold DEF for about 0.5 s using fixed_kp 60 and fixed_kd 5, as rl_sar's GetUp state does.
   - Switch to the policy with a zero history and zero last_action.
13. Command interface for the higher-level controller: cmd = [vx, vy, wz] in body frame, units m/s, m/s and rad/s. Default is [0,0,0]. rl_sar's gamepad envelope is [-1,1] per axis; clamp to it, because the trained range is unknown.
14. If the robot stumbles: first rerun with hip action scale 0.25 (the original deployment config for this same file), then try the timestep 0.002 fallback.

Alternative policy, robot_lab/policy.pt (clean Apache-2.0 licence, but not exercised by rl_sar for Go2): 45 inputs and no history. Observation order: [gyro*0.25, g, cmd*1.0, (q-DEF)*1.0, dq*0.05, last_action]. Policy order FR,FL,RR,RL, so JM is the identity and q comes from sensordata[0:12]. DEF = [0,0.8,-1.5]x4, action_scale = [0.125,0.25,0.25]x4. rl_sar uses kp 20 / kd 0.5, but robot_lab trained with 25 / 0.5. Same 0.005 s dt and decimation 4.

----- go2_proof.py -----
# rl_sar go2/himloco policy in headless MuJoCo, CPU. Usage: python go2_proof.py [hip_action_scale=0.125] [timestep=0.005]
import hashlib, os, re, sys, time, urllib.request
import numpy as np, mujoco, torch

RL = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fan-ziqi/rl_sar/376d42c9b128f963ab08579762d5a216a976ce39/policy/go2/himloco/himloco.pt"
UM = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_mujoco/1eb6642e3f3fdfb7fb13a9794fd6a2dd93ea0e7d/unitree_robots/go2/go2.xml"
D = "dl"; os.makedirs(D, exist_ok=True)
def fetch(url, name, sha):
    p = os.path.join(D, name)
    if not os.path.exists(p): urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, p)
    b = open(p, "rb").read(); assert hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest() == sha, name
    return b
pt = fetch(RL, "himloco.pt", "d9945f85a39944aaf241a67f7d2b25a15326a0222d0e503aeb05a7f188430509")
xml = fetch(UM, "go2.xml", "2014a3d76e30f17ab9447d8a67bd015291f74fa4d71ae30d005f1a32bd693d4b").decode()
# strip visual meshes (contype=0, bodies have explicit <inertial>, so physics unchanged) -> no .obj downloads
xml = re.sub(r'<mesh [^>]*/>|<geom [^>]*mesh="[^"]*"[^>]*/>', "", xml)
xml = xml.replace("</worldbody>", '<geom name="floor" size="0 0 0.05" type="plane"/></worldbody>', 1)
m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string(xml); d = mujoco.MjData(m)

HIP = float(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 0.125
m.opt.timestep = float(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 0.005
DEC = round(0.02 / m.opt.timestep)                    # policy period = dt 0.005 * decimation 4
JM = np.array([3, 4, 5, 0, 1, 2, 9, 10, 11, 6, 7, 8])  # policy joint i <-> actuator/sensor JM[i]
DEF = np.array([0.1, 0.8, -1.5, -0.1, 0.8, -1.5, 0.1, 1.0, -1.5, -0.1, 1.0, -1.5])
SCALE = np.array([HIP, 0.25, 0.25] * 4)
LEGS = ["FL", "FR", "RL", "RR"]; PARTS = ["hip", "thigh", "calf"]
assert [m.actuator(int(j)).name for j in JM] == [f"{l}_{p}" for l in LEGS for p in PARTS]
assert [m.joint(i + 1).name for i in range(12)] == [f"{l}_{p}_joint" for l in LEGS for p in PARTS]
assert m.nsensordata == 52 and m.nu == 12

def sense():
    s = d.sensordata
    return s[JM], s[12 + JM], s[36:40], s[40:43]      # q, dq (policy order), quat wxyz, gyro (body)
def grav(qt):                                          # rl_sar QuatRotateInverse(q, [0,0,-1])
    w, u, v = qt[0], qt[1:], np.array([0.0, 0.0, -1.0])
    return v * (2 * w * w - 1) - np.cross(u, v) * w * 2 + u * np.dot(u, v) * 2
def pd(qdes, kp, kd):
    q, dq, _, _ = sense()
    d.ctrl[JM] = kp * (qdes - q) - kd * dq             # MuJoCo clamps to ctrlrange 23.7 / 45.43

d.qpos[:7] = [0, 0, 0.35, 1, 0, 0, 0]; d.qpos[7:19] = DEF; mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
for _ in range(int(0.5 / m.opt.timestep)):            # stand with fixed_kp 60 / fixed_kd 5
    pd(DEF, 60.0, 5.0); mujoco.mj_step(m, d)

torch.set_num_threads(1)
pol = torch.jit.load(os.path.join(D, "himloco.pt"), map_location="cpu").eval()
hist = np.zeros((6, 45), np.float32); act = np.zeros(12, np.float32)
cmd = np.array([0.5, 0.0, 0.0])                       # vx m/s, vy m/s, yaw rad/s
x0, y0, N, t0 = d.qpos[0], d.qpos[1], 250, time.perf_counter()
for k in range(N):                                     # 5 s at 50 Hz
    q, dq, qt, gyro = sense()
    obs = np.concatenate([cmd * [2.0, 2.0, 0.25], gyro * 0.25, grav(qt), (q - DEF) * 1.0, dq * 0.05, act])
    hist = np.roll(hist, 1, 0); hist[0] = np.clip(obs, -100, 100)   # newest first
    with torch.no_grad():
        a = pol(torch.from_numpy(hist.reshape(1, 270))).numpy()[0]
    act = np.clip(a, -100, 100).astype(np.float32)
    qdes = act * SCALE + DEF
    for _ in range(DEC):
        pd(qdes, 40.0, 1.0); mujoco.mj_step(m, d)
    if d.qpos[2] < 0.15: break
wall = time.perf_counter() - t0
dx, dy, z, gz = d.qpos[0] - x0, d.qpos[1] - y0, d.qpos[2], grav(sense()[2])[2]
print(f"hip={HIP} ts={m.opt.timestep} steps={k + 1} dx={dx:.2f}m dy={dy:.2f}m z={z:.3f}m gz={gz:.2f} realtime_x={(k + 1) * 0.02 / wall:.1f}")
print("PASS" if k + 1 == N and dx > 1.0 and abs(dy) < 0.5 and z > 0.2 and gz < -0.8 else "FAIL")

(3) mj_geomDistance(m, d, geom1, geom2, distmax, fromto) returns a Python float. fromto is a writable float64 array of 6 values, or None. Two spheres give 0.2 as expected, and the result is negative when they overlap.

(4) mujoco.Renderer produces an offscreen 240x320x3 uint8 frame. On Windows the only backend is GLFW with a hidden window (VISIBLE=0) on WGL, here the Intel HD Graphics 620 OpenGL 4.5 driver. Setting MUJOCO_GL=egl or osmesa makes `import mujoco` itself fail with a RuntimeError. With mujoco-core alone, Renderer() raises ImportError for missing glfw; the documented fix is mujoco-core[rendering] or the full mujoco package, and I verified that fix renders.

(5) qpos after 2000 steps is byte-identical across fresh data, fresh model, reused data and two separate processes. It is not identical across versions (3.17.0 gives a different hash).

(6) Writing m.geom_friction and m.opt.gravity takes effect on the next step without recompiling. However, the Go2 foot geoms have priority=1, so changing only the floor friction has no effect on foot-floor contacts (friction stays 0.8). To vary ground friction, change the foot geoms' friction or raise the floor's priority.

(7) Contacts can be read as geom-id pairs from d.contact.geom[:d.ncon] (in either order) and forces from mj_contactForce.

(8) In the Go2 scene: timestep 0.002, 12 actuators that are direct torque motors (gain 1, no bias; ctrl is in Nm). Joint order and actuator order are both FL, FR, RL, RR × hip, thigh, calf. The 'home' keyframe ctrl (0, 0.9, -1.8 per leg) is therefore applied as torques. The floor has friction [1, 0.005, 0.0001]. Single-thread throughput with zero control is about 9,000-10,000 steps/s (real-time factor about 18-20x).

import sys, time, numpy as np, mujoco
scene = sys.argv[1]
print("mujoco", mujoco.__version__, "numpy", np.__version__)
m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path(scene); d = mujoco.MjData(m)
# 8. Go2 facts
legs = [f"{l}_{p}" for l in ("FL", "FR", "RL", "RR") for p in ("hip", "thigh", "calf")]
assert (m.opt.timestep, m.nq, m.nv, m.nu) == (0.002, 19, 18, 12)
assert [m.actuator(i).name for i in range(m.nu)] == legs
assert [m.joint(m.actuator_trnid[i, 0]).name for i in range(m.nu)] == [n + "_joint" for n in legs]
assert all(m.actuator_gaintype == mujoco.mjtGain.mjGAIN_FIXED) and all(m.actuator_biastype == mujoco.mjtBias.mjBIAS_NONE)
assert np.allclose(m.key_qpos[0], [0, 0, 0.27, 1, 0, 0, 0] + [0, 0.9, -1.8] * 4)
floor, fl = m.geom("floor").id, m.geom("FL").id
assert np.allclose(m.geom_friction[floor], [1, 0.005, 0.0001]) and m.geom_priority[fl] == 1
# 2. MjSpec: add a body with geom and mass before compiling
spec = mujoco.MjSpec.from_file(scene)
b = spec.worldbody.add_body(name="obstacle", pos=[1, 0, 0.1]); b.add_freejoint()
b.add_geom(name="obstacle_geom", type=mujoco.mjtGeom.mjGEOM_BOX, size=[0.1, 0.1, 0.1], mass=2.5)
m2 = spec.compile(); assert m2.nbody == m.nbody + 1 and m2.body_mass[m2.body("obstacle").id] == 2.5
# 3. mj_geomDistance on two spheres (radii 0.1 and 0.2, centres 0.5 apart)
ms = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string('<mujoco><worldbody><geom type="sphere" size="0.1"/>'
                                    '<geom type="sphere" size="0.2" pos="0.5 0 0"/></worldbody></mujoco>')
ds = mujoco.MjData(ms); mujoco.mj_forward(ms, ds); ft = np.zeros(6)
dist = mujoco.mj_geomDistance(ms, ds, 0, 1, 10.0, ft); assert abs(dist - 0.2) < 1e-9, dist
print("geomDistance", dist, "fromto", ft)
# 4. offscreen render, no visible window
r = mujoco.Renderer(m, 240, 320); mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(m, d, 0); mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
r.update_scene(d); img = r.render(); assert img.shape == (240, 320, 3) and img.std() > 5
print("render ok via", mujoco.GLContext.__module__, img.shape, img.dtype); r.close()
# 5. bit-identical qpos after 2000 steps, twice
def run():
    dd = mujoco.MjData(m); mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(m, dd, 0)
    for _ in range(2000): mujoco.mj_step(m, dd)
    return dd.qpos.tobytes()
assert run() == run(); print("determinism ok")
# 6. friction: foot priority=1 wins over floor; gravity change takes effect immediately
def fl_floor_friction():
    mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(m, d, 0); mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
    return [c.friction[0] for c in d.contact[:d.ncon] if {c.geom1, c.geom2} == {floor, fl}][0]
m.geom_friction[floor, 0] = 0.2; assert fl_floor_friction() == 0.8
m.geom_priority[floor] = 2; assert abs(fl_floor_friction() - 0.2) < 1e-12
m.geom_priority[floor] = 0; m.geom_friction[floor, 0] = 1.0
mb = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_string('<mujoco><worldbody><body><freejoint/><geom size="0.1"/></body></worldbody></mujoco>')
mb.opt.gravity[:] = [3.0, 0, -9.0]; db = mujoco.MjData(mb); mujoco.mj_forward(mb, db)
assert np.allclose(db.qacc[:3], [3.0, 0, -9.0]); print("friction/gravity ok")
# 7. contacts between named geoms
mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(m, d, 0); mujoco.mj_forward(m, d)
pairs = d.contact.geom[:d.ncon]
assert any({int(a), int(b)} == {floor, fl} for a, b in pairs); print("contacts", [(m.geom(int(a)).name, m.geom(int(b)).name) for a, b in pairs])
# 8. throughput, zero control, single thread
mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(m, d, 0); d.ctrl[:] = 0; t = time.perf_counter()
for _ in range(10000): mujoco.mj_step(m, d)
sps = 10000 / (time.perf_counter() - t); print(f"steps/s {sps:.0f}  real-time factor {sps * m.opt.timestep:.1f}x")
print("PROOF_OK")

Facts the environment code should rely on:
1. Pin all three packages to the same version: `mujoco==4.0.1 mujoco-core==4.0.1 mujoco-studio==4.0.1 numpy==2.5.5`. A slimmer equivalent is `mujoco-core[rendering]==4.0.1`. Fallback: `mujoco==3.17.0`, which shows the same behaviour here. Never set MUJOCO_GL=egl or osmesa on Windows. Leave it unset, or set glfw or wgl.
2. Load with m = mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path('<menagerie@370c439>/unitree_go2/scene.xml'), then d = mujoco.MjData(m) and mujoco.mj_resetDataKeyframe(m, d, 0). After reset, overwrite d.ctrl: the keyframe ctrl is applied as torques.
3. State layout: qpos[0:3] base position, qpos[3:7] base quaternion (w,x,y,z), qpos[7:19] joints, qvel[0:6] base, qvel[6:18] joints. Joint and actuator order are both FL, FR, RL, RR × hip, thigh, calf. Actuators are torque motors (ctrl in Nm), clamped to ±23.7 for hip and thigh and ±45.43 for calf. A position-target policy needs ctrl = clip(kp*(q_target - q) - kd*qd) every sim step. At dt=0.002, a 50 Hz policy means 10 mj_step calls per action.
4. To add obstacles: MjSpec.from_file, then worldbody.add_body / add_freejoint / add_geom(mass=...), then compile(), then build a new MjData. Bodies appended after the robot leave robot indices unchanged.
5. Ground friction: write m.geom_friction for the foot geoms ('FL', 'FR', 'RL', 'RR', priority 1), or set m.geom_priority[floor] = 2. Writing only the floor friction has no effect on foot contacts. Gravity: m.opt.gravity[:] = vec. Both changes apply on the next step.
6. Contacts: compare d.contact.geom[:d.ncon] against the pair in either order; get force with mujoco.mj_contactForce(m, d, i, f6), where f6[0] is the normal force.
7. Distance queries: mujoco.mj_geomDistance(m, d, g1, g2, distmax, fromto6_or_None) -> float; it returns distmax when nothing is closer.
8. Rendering: r = mujoco.Renderer(m, h <= 480, w <= 640); r.update_scene(d[, camera]); r.render() returns uint8 HxWx3. Use it from one thread only.
9. Expect about 9-10k steps/s single-threaded (about 18-20x real time), and bit-identical replays within one mujoco version.

missing: Free-joint velocity frames are not stated. I measured them: qvel[0:3] is base linear velocity in the WORLD frame, and qvel[3:6] is base angular velocity in the BODY (local) frame. With the base yawed 90°, qvel lin [1,0,0] stayed world [1,0,0] while ang [1,0,0] became world [0,1,0]. A policy that expects body-frame linear velocity or projected gravity must rotate these with the qpos[3:7] (w,x,y,z) quaternion.

go2.xml has nsensor 0: no gyro, accelerometer or framequat. Only the 'imu' site (id 0) exists. The environment must compute IMU-like observations from qpos/qvel or add sensors with MjSpec. go2_mjx.xml does define gyro, accelerometer, framequat, framepos, framelinvel and frameangvel on the imu site, and its sensor list orders legs FL, RL, FR, RR, which is not the actuator order.

The policy's observation layout, scales, default joint angles, action scale, control rate and PD gains are not established; the report lists this as an open question. For go2.xml torque motors, no working kp/kd is given. The report's kp=30, kd=0.5 PD hold sags from base z 0.27 to 0.2076.

The two model variants differ in ways that matter for sim-to-sim transfer, and the report covers this only in part. go2_mjx.xml joints have no frictionloss (go2.xml has 0.2). Its foot spheres have radius 0.0175 and solimp 0.015 1 0.031 (go2.xml: 0.022 and 0.015 1 0.022). It disables eulerdamp, and its position-target ctrlranges are abduction ±0.9472, front thigh [-1.4, 2.5], back thigh [-0.4236, 2.5] and calf [-2.6227, -0.84776].
